picks.file: Gezicht op Smyrna met op de voorgrond de ontvangst van de Nederlandse consul Daniël Jan Baron de Hochepied (1657-1723) in de Divan, SK-A-4085.jpg
picks.why: detailed colored bird’s-eye of the town under Mount Pagos and its castle; trimmed to the city, cutting the consul’s reception scene below; dated by the consul’s term

picks.what: The city from the sea with Mount Pagos, painting (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: dated general view along the waterfront, Kadifekale ruins on the hill at right; larger copy of #7

picks.file: View of the Town and Bay of Smyrna (1829) by Raffael Corsini (PEM M25790).jpg
picks.what: The town and bay from the sea, painting (Peabody Essex Museum)
picks.why: colorful panorama of the town and the crowded harbor, 50 years after #6; title strip cut

picks.what: The town and harbor from the hillside, photograph
picks.why: firmly dated general view over the roofs to the bay and anchored ships; bare foreground cut
quay and harbor two years after the 1922 fire; weak on landmarks but the only ordinary view for the period

picks.what: The city and the gulf from Kadifekale, photograph
picks.why: sharp modern panorama over the old town to the Gulf of İzmir

notes: P2 alternatives: Cornelis de Bruijn’s large engraved panorama (#4, very high resolution, probably from his 1698 travel book but undated on Commons) and Tournefort’s 1717 plate (#5, small). P4: #12 (1880s, larger) is a good alternative looking toward Kadifekale; #15 is a stylized Ottoman lithograph. P5: Mittelholzer’s ruins photos (#21, #22) would need event marking; left out.
